title: Intake gating and remediation lanes for private/VPC requests with intermittent egress
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We are receiving an increasing number of private/VPC/on-prem deployment requests from enterprise customers that report intermittent or transient egress (corporate proxies, scheduled maintenance windows, and air-gapped sync windows). Current intake funnels funnel them into a single 'network readiness' lane which creates long handoffs for Eng and Support and leads to missed expectations and surprise rollbacks during staged upgrades.

Goal: Define a lightweight, automated intake gating and remediation lane matrix that:
- Quickly classifies requests by risk and automation feasibility;
- Offers predictable runbooks and self-serve probes for low/medium risk customers;
- Provides clear escalation and concierge lanes for high-risk or legally constrained customers;
- Integrates with existing preflight probes, Onboarding Console, and support routing so SLAs and runbooks are consistent.

Proposed approach:
1) Intake classifier: collect a minimal signal set at form submission (eggress schedule windows, proxy type, TLS interception, firewall egress FQDN allowlist feasibility, upgrade blackout windows, legal/regulatory constraints).
2) Scoring rubric (example dimensions and weights): Network maturity (30%), Upgrade risk window complexity (20%), Legal/regulatory constraints (20%), Automation feasibility (15%), Business priority (15%). Each dimension scored 0-5, weighted sum produces lane: Self-serve, Assisted, Concierge.
3) Automated probe kit: a downloadable ephemeral probe that customers run inside their network (opt-in, short-lived token) that performs egress checks and returns a summarized, privacy-safe result to the intake record. Probe must be read-only and not collect PII.
4) Remediation lanes: map scoring outputs to remediation templates and SLOs: Self-serve -> automated checklist + docs + 3-day SLA; Assisted -> scheduled network session with SRE + 5-day SLA; Concierge -> dedicated onboarding, contract amendment review, and prioritized engineering runway.
5) Upgrade gating: add a required 'upgrade window compatibility' boolean for customers wanting staged rollout; failing compatibility triggers mandatory Assisted lane.

Acceptance criteria:
- Form updated to capture minimal signals and feed the classifier (UX copy reviewed).
- Scoring rubric documented and agreed by Eng, Security, and Solutions (doc link attached).
- Probe kit prototype exists and passes security checklist (no persistent telemetry).
- Routing rules implemented in intake router to map lanes to Support/SE/SRE queues.
- Pilot with three customers (one self-serve, one assisted, one concierge) completed and lessons logged.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Privacy vs automation: probe kit reduces manual work but requires explicit customer opt-in and strong data minimization. Security team requires a formal review before enabling probes.
- False negatives: scoring may misclassify nuanced cases; will include 'manual reclassify' option for Support.
- Engineering capacity: Assisted/Concierge lanes will increase Eng time; compensate with clearer runbooks and templated remediation.

Next deliverables (short-term):
- Finalize form fields and sample scoring weights (this ticket).
- Confluence PRD linked in attachments.
- Security review kickoff (request to Security team).
- Implementation story split for Intake UI, Probe kit eng spike, Router rules, Runbook authoring.
